value.note: closed-loop 1:1 absolute pointer (artistctl / qemu-artist-closedloop): the Artist hardware-cursor registers are the sensor, SH_CURSOR_SCALE is inert. Foreign-arch TCG station on /opt/qemu-hppa (kernel-hive fork), like macos753. No network exec channel, but a serial console getty on tty1p0 gives a root shell on serve/serial.sock (docs/lab/retronet/WEB-STATION-hpuxvue.md).

labctl.notes: exec = serial_shell: the golden bakes a LIVE root session on the guest's serial line (-sh on tty1p0, PS1 KHPROMPT>, reached on serial.sock in the station dir) -- there is NO getty to log in to, and Mosaic (a window of the exhibit scene) is a CHILD of that shell, so the client must never end the session. Client scripts/labctl.d/hpuxvueexec.py, no port, no password. MEASURED LIMIT: shell builtins are reliable (120/120 echo, 20/20 append+readback, 10/10 forking subshells) but running an EXTERNAL binary wedges the session about half the time, permanently -- the tty still echoes, nothing executes, and no getty respawns because init's respawn slot is held by the shell that is still there. exec reports a wedge as exit 125; the heal is `labctl reset hpuxvue` (loadvm golden), which also resets the visitor's scene, so it is the operator's call. A wedge does NOT stall the guest: the closed-loop pointer still converges exactly. See docs/guests/hpuxvue.md. POINTER ACCURACY: WITHIN 1 px, NOT EXACT. The Artist engine is a closed loop with ptr-deadband=1 and converges on abs(err) <= deadband on BOTH axes, so it is SPECIFIED to stop within one pixel -- `labctl abs x y` lands at x+/-1, y+/-1, converged and held. This is weaker than rhapsody's and macos753's exact landing: those use kh-ramabs, which has no deadband at all and tests literal equality, so 0 px is the correct strictness there and 1 px would hide a missed publish. Do not carry this tolerance to a ramabs station, and do not set ptr-deadband=0 to make a test pass -- the deadband is what stops the hunting that leaves window-border hotspots unmeasurable.

render.stationsManifestPrelude:
# hpuxvue (slot 144) — HP-UX 10.20 / HP VUE on a PA-RISC HP 9000/778 (B160L):
#   qemu-system-hppa from the kernel-hive QEMU fork, installed to /opt/qemu-hppa
#   (pve-qemu ships no hppa target). TCG only, no KVM. Artist framebuffer
#   scanout at 1280x1024 (HARD ceiling: higher crashes / dtwm pointer dead zone).
#   CLOSED-LOOP 1:1 pointer (artistctl over artistptr/1): the wire is still the
#   LASI PS/2 mouse, but the engine in hw/display/artist.c reads the guest's own
#   position back from the Artist hardware-cursor registers and converges on it.
#   LISTED on the public floor: reset=loadvm golden, idle auto-pause after
#   SH_IDLE_PAUSE_SECS=60.

deviceSetSummary: -chardev socket,id=ptr0,path=$D/ptr.sock,server=on,wait=off -global artist.ptrctl=ptr0 (the closed-loop pointer engine's control socket in hw/display/artist.c; the daemon speaks artistptr/1 over it)
-drive if=scsi,bus=0,index=2,media=cdrom,file=$A/disc1.iso (always attached; -boot d only in the install shape)

launcherParity.reason: tracked verbatim launcher IS the deployed launcher; the golden checkpoint (re-baked 2026-08-24) was captured with this exact device set (CD attached, same ISO) on the standalone /opt/qemu-hppa build. The closed-loop pointer was then ARMED without a re-bake, and does not need one: the engine in hw/display/artist.c adds no migration state (cursor_pos/cursor_cntrl were already in vmstate_artist) and the ptrctl chardev is a backend, not a vmstate section, so the device set is unchanged for loadvm purposes and the 2026-08-24 golden still restores -- RESTORE-PROVEN under this binary with the loop armed, on the sandbox ptrloop rig. binarySha256 is the build this branch's 0008-artist-closed-loop-pointer.patch produces (kernel-hive + that patch); it is NOT yet what /opt/qemu-hppa holds, because this branch is not deployed. INSTALL ORDER MATTERS: the QEMU binary must be in place BEFORE this launcher, because -global artist.ptrctl=ptr0 on the previous binary is an unknown property and QEMU refuses to start; likewise the streamhost binary before the env fixture (SH_INPUT_BACKEND=artistctl panics an older daemon).

qemuBuild.note: Built from fork c5449c80 with 0008 only -- 0006 is rhapsody's x86 i8259 fix and does not apply to hppa. binarySha256 read from the INSTALLED file, not a build log. RESTORE-PROVEN on the live station: loadvm golden succeeded under this binary with -global artist.ptrctl=ptr0 accepted on a real machine start, running inode equal to the on-disk inode. That start is also the only available validation of the ptrctl property: an argument-only probe cannot distinguish a valid property from an invalid one, because QEMU's chardev check runs first. Previous binary kept as <path>.pre-abs-bak (76ef7ce9...), which has ZERO ptrctl strings -- the launcher passes -global artist.ptrctl unconditionally, so binary and launcher roll back together or not at all.

museum.blurb: HP’s own Visual User Environment — the Motif desktop that CDE was built from — on the PA-RISC workstation Unix of the HP 9000 line.
museum.notes: Second non-CDE Motif workstation desktop in the hall (HP VUE 3.0 — what CDE was derived from); PA-RISC under TCG on a standalone qemu-system-hppa build.

network.note: retronet web plane: the tulip is a REAL bridged NIC on vmbr-rn via the persistent tap hpuxrn0 (streamhost/stations/hpuxvue/rn-tapnet.sh), MAC RN_HPUXVUE_MAC, HP-UX driver btlan3 as lan0. Addressed 10.99.0.20/24 with DNS 10.99.0.2 and NO default gateway — static, not DHCP, because the June-1996 dhcpclient cannot enumerate the btlan3 PPA (docs/lab/retronet/WEB-STATION-hpuxvue.md). Contained by the fail-closed HPUXRN-IN chain: reaches the gateway CT only, never labhost, the LAN or the internet.
